deviations: D1 (Tenant resolution for GetOrderByCode): Used tenant-filtered query (X-Fleet-Slug header required) + ownership check (CustomerUserId == sub), NOT IgnoreQueryFilters(). This matches WI-08's customer create/read pattern which also requires X-Fleet-Slug. Rationale: PublicCode is unique per-fleet only (index: fleet_id, public_code), so an unscoped IgnoreQueryFilters cross-fleet lookup would be ambiguous by schema. Cross-fleet tracking without fleet context is deferred to the signed-token path in assignment 05.

D2 (GetByCode requires X-Fleet-Slug): Customer JWT carries no fleet_id claim. The X-Fleet-Slug header is mandatory to resolve the tenant (same requirement as create-order for customers in WI-08). Tests set client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Add('X-Fleet-Slug', fleet.Slug) on all customer clients. Documented in endpoint Summary.

D3 (TrackOrderResponse fields): Reduced DTO exposes: publicCode, status, pickupAddress, dropoffAddress, scheduledAt, driverFirstName (first token of DisplayName), vehiclePlate, vehicleColor, etaMinutes (always null v1), position (DriverPositionDto{lat,lng} | null — only when status is Accepted/Arrived/InProgress and LastLat/LastLng non-null). Fields intentionally absent: customerPhone, customerName, all price fields (*Czk), allowedActions, order IDs beyond publicCode.
D4 (EtaMinutes always null in v1): OSRM integration is assignment 06 scope. Field is present in DTO with null value and documented in Summary as 'always null in v1'.

D5 (GetOrderEvents payload projection): Cannot project JsonDocument.RootElement.Clone() inside an EF Core LINQ-to-SQL query. Events are loaded with ToListAsync() first, then mapped to OrderEventDto in memory. JsonDocument disposal is safe — Clone() produces an independent copy that does not depend on the original document lifetime.

D6 (AddNote SaveChanges): AddNoteEndpoint calls dbContext.SaveChangesAsync directly — it does NOT use OrderService.TransitionAsync because NoteAdded is not a state-machine transition (no status change, no driver status update, no concurrency token bump). The SaveChanges guard in TaxiDbContext still fires and will enforce the FleetId on the new OrderEvent row.

D7 (GetByCode_CrossTenantCode_Returns404 test): Green on arrival — the tenant filter mechanism was already proven by WI-04. This test proves that the by-code code lookup is scoped to the fleet of the X-Fleet-Slug header, not just to the owner's fleet, and that the correct owner under the wrong fleet context also receives 404.
D8 (micro-fix pass F1): DriverPositionDto moved from TrackOrderResponse.cs into its own file DriverPositionDto.cs per architecture#one-type-per-file.

D9 (micro-fix pass F3): GetOrderEventsEndpoint now disposes the original pooled JsonDocument buffers after all clones have been taken via 'foreach (var raw in rawEvents) raw.Payload?.Dispose();'. Placed after the materialized events list is built so Clone() has already completed.

D10 (micro-fix pass F2): Added GetByCode_AssignedDriverActiveStatus_ReturnsFirstNameAndPosition test. Uses ASCII two-token name 'Tomas Horak', asserts first name present + surname absent from raw JSON, position null for Assigned status (non-active), position object with exact lat/lng for Accepted status (active). Test was green on first run — behavior was already correct (code-inspected by reviewer); discriminating signal comes from strong positive assertions (exact values, null/object ValueKind check).
